title: Local Models: Trust, Control, Optimization — Carter Abdallah, NVIDIA
talk_summary: A panel of open-model lab leaders (Prime Intellect, RC, NVIDIA Nemotron) argues that open-weight models plus post-training on your own harness and production traces yields cheaper, more controllable, specialized agents than closed frontier APIs. It is mostly strategic advocacy; the only concrete mechanisms are harness-specific post-training, trace collection for a data flywheel, and matching model size to task rather than defaulting to frontier models.

takeaways.technique: Match model size to task, not frontier-by-default
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue most tasks do not need frontier intelligence and that a model specialized for one or two tasks at the expense of everything else is more effective and cheaper.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most people probably do not need frontier level intelligence for like 90% of their tasks
takeaways.numbers: 90% of tasks claimed not to need frontier

takeaways.technique: Post-train/evaluate against your own harness, not generic benchmarks
takeaways.what_they_do: Claim models are benchmarked across many harnesses but you only use one, so specializing a model to your harness beats a general model; cite a finance company specializing an open model in 1-2 weeks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can do things like news research can create a post train of whatever model for their harness
takeaways.numbers: finance agent specialized in 1-2 weeks, beating Opus at a fraction of Haiku cost (vendor claim)

takeaways.technique: Collect production traces as a data flywheel
takeaways.what_they_do: Save all traces of agents running in your harness so you can later fine-tune a smaller model or mine signals for RL environments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you're using an open model, you can save all of those traces

takeaways.technique: Own the inference stack to control cost predictability
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue closed APIs carry margin and can raise prices or deprecate models, while open models plus vLLM-class serving let you drive cost down and pass savings through.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they might drive down the optimization, but then might not pass through those savings

takeaways.technique: Specialized model swarms over one general model
takeaways.what_they_do: Predict a shift from single general models to systems of specialized models per domain.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Swarms of or specialized systems of models, I think you're going to be increasingly important
